newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end weaker, Telefonica gives support.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end weaker, Telefonica gives support.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended slightly lower in dull trade on Monday amid low volume and bond market losses, dealers said.
The general index fell 1.12 points, 0.29 percent, to 381.68 and the Ibex dropped 13.29 points, 0.3 percent, to 4,383.62.
Details of the government's privatisation calendar prompted interest in key stocks. Telefonica rose 35 pesetas to 2,645, supporting the Ibex, while Repsol fell 65 pesetas to 4,130.
The government said at the weekend that it will place its 21 percent in the telephone operator around the start of 1997, and its 10 percent stake in the energy firm in the following months.
Santander fell 60 pesetas to 6,700 after nine-month results which analysts said were in line with forecasts, although they underperformed other banks' results.
"Except in two or three stocks, it's been quiet with Telefonica clearly the protagonist, while Tabacalera and Repsol saw clear selling," said a dealer.
Tabacalera fell 5 percent amid talk of the possibility that the Portuguese government may chose Philip Morris over the Spanish tobacco firm for a stake in Tabaquiera.
Telefonica and Repsol accounted for 40 percent of volume. RTR LOL
